text:
opsbot: ALERT: gpu.errors.ecc spike detected across fleet in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Impact: ~14% capacity reduction, increased inference 5xx. Rule: gpu.errors.ecc > 50/min for 5m. See telemetry dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood/api/d/health/gpu-errors

maya: seeing same in infra dashboard, nodes in two AZs show correlated ECC counts. Not limited to a single SKU.

alex: quick snapshot of logs from node gpu-node-472: ```[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] ECC_ERROR: device=0 count=3 pci_slot=0000:04:00.0 xid=31 pci_reset_attempts=1```

maya: xid=31 repeats, then a soft reset, then more ECC. Looks like noisy card rather than firmware push.

jen: is there any recent BIOS/driver rollout? I can't find a cluster-wide driver bump in the last 48h. Only small perf agent update.

alex: confirmed no driver rollouts. Kernel patch landed last week but only on canaries.

leo: can we cordon nodes with >10 ECC errors/min and force jobs off them? Proposal: kubectl cordon && drain with --ignore-daemonsets and evict gracefully. Risk: capacity hit ~8% further.

maya: do it. Start with a small batch (10% of affected nodes) and watch inference 95th latency. If we see tail latency spike, halt and fall back to cross-region routing.

opsbot: EXEC: kubectl drain gpu-node-472 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 -> SUCCESS

alex: started automated cordon+drain job targeting nodes with gpu.errors.ecc_rate > 20/m. Job run id: drain-20260318-01.

jen: I'm updating the incident ticket with a mitigation plan and owner. We should also schedule hardware RMA for nodes with repeated ECC after drain. Vendor RMA window is 72h, need priority for prod fleet.

simon: quick thought: enable KV cache warmup on remaining nodes to reduce bursts and token churn while capacity is lowered. Also temporarily reduce batch sizes in endpoint routing to lower memory pressure.

maya: implementing batch-size override via routing policy: set max_batch_tokens=1024 for high-priority routes. Pushing change now.

alex: note: telemetry shows a small population of older HBM cards in racks 12-15 with voltage drift events. I'm opening a rack-level ticket with datacenter ops. Could be power rail noise causing ECC.

leo: cost question — if we fallback to us-east for load, we'll spin up dedicated spare capacity. Approx cost: $18k/day if sustained. Ops approval?

jen: approve emergency capacity up to $5k/day for next 48h. Anything beyond needs exec signoff.

maya: update: after draining 30 nodes, ECC error rate dropped 78% in us-west-2, application 5xx reduced to baseline. Still seeing intermittent small spikes in eu-central-1; targeting 8 nodes there next.

opsbot: NOTE: automated RMA candidate list generated: [gpu-node-472, gpu-node-501, gpu-node-534, gpu-node-590]. RMA ticket: RMA-8342.

alex: plan for next 24h: 1) finish targeted drains in eu-central-1, 2) schedule physical inspection for racks 12-15, 3) keep batch-size override in place for 6h, 4) monitor telemetry and rollback if latency regresses.

simon: +1. Also adding an alert annotation in dashboard about temporary routing policy to avoid alert churn.

jen: I'll coordinate communications with support and customers if there are prolonged degradations. For now mark incident as "mitigating".

maya: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:

leo: FYI, I'll follow up with finance about the emergency capacity spend and provide a delta report by EOD.

opsbot: RESOLVE CHECK: after last action, gpu.errors.ecc aggregated across fleet at 00:35 UTC down to 12/m -> below alert threshold. Closing escalation if stable for 30m.

maya: monitoring window started. If stable after 30m we can un-cordon low-risk nodes gradually.

jen: closing notes will go into postmortem template once stabilized.

simon: adding note: consider increasing pre-shipment burn-in tests for GPUs from vendor for future batches (longer thermal cycles).
